about: A Greek invocation for mercy. Three repetitions of “Kýrie eléison” lead to three of “Christe eléison”, after which “Kýrie eléison” returns three more times.

s01.narrative: The priest returns to the middle of the altar and alternates the invocations with the server: Kýrie three times, Christe three times, Kýrie three times. At a sung Mass the choir sings them, while the priest says them at the Epistle side, alternating with the ministers.

w001.function: A vocative, as in the Greek: κύριε from κύριος. The ending is the same -e as in “Christe” (w007).

w002.function: An imperative: “have mercy”. The Greek here is an aorist — it asks for the act of mercy taken whole rather than as a continuing state — a distinction the Latin imperative cannot draw, and the Polish perfective “zmiłuj się” happens to keep.

w007.function: A vocative of “Christus” — the same ending as “Kýrie”, and still Greek: this invocation was composed at Rome, and the Greeks do not use it in their liturgy.
